biography:
Ray Shahi's journey from the dusty backroads of Arizona to the gleaming circuits of international GT racing is a testament to raw talent and relentless determination. Born to immigrant parents who ran a small auto repair shop, Ray practically grew up with a wrench in his hand, learning the mechanics of speed before he even had a driver's license. His racing career began in local dirt track events, where his aggressive style quickly earned him a reputation – and a few wrecked cars. A defining moment came at a regional race where, despite starting last due to engine trouble, he clawed his way to victory in a borrowed, beat-up stock car. 

This raw performance caught the attention of a small-time sports car team owner, who offered Ray his first shot at professional racing. The transition wasn't easy; the precision of sports car racing demanded a level of finesse Ray initially lacked. But his innate speed and willingness to learn quickly closed the gap. After several successful years in GT4, he landed a coveted spot with the Lamborghini factory team, a dream come true for the young American. 

However, things haven't been easy in the top flight. While flashes of brilliance are evident, consistent results have been elusive, due to both car issues and Ray's own aggressive driving style pushing the boundaries of the machinery. Despite the challenges, Ray remains undeterred, fueled by an unwavering belief in his ability to reach the pinnacle of GT racing. He is currently focused on refining his racecraft and finding the consistency needed to compete for championships.
drivingStyle: Ray Shahi's driving style is best described as 'controlled aggression.' He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and fearless corner entries, often pushing the car right to the edge of grip. While his raw speed is undeniable, he sometimes struggles with tire management, often burning through his rubber early in a stint due to his aggressive driving. He thrives under pressure, however, and is known for pulling off daring overtakes in the closing laps of races.

rivalries.name: Marco Bellini
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their days in GT4, where their aggressive driving styles often led to on-track collisions and heated exchanges. Bellini represents the established European guard Ray is trying to dethrone.

rivalries.name: Anya Petrova
rivalries.reason: Petrova, known for her ice-cold composure and strategic brilliance, frequently outsmarts Ray on track. Their rivalry is more of a tactical one, with Ray often trying to disrupt Petrova's calculated approach with aggressive moves.

rivalries.name: Kenji 'Kaze' Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka, a Japanese driver known for his incredible car control, is often the target of Shahi's over-ambitious overtaking attempts, leading to many on-track clashes.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky wristband his father gave him before every race.
Listens to heavy metal at full volume in the garage right before getting into the car.
Refuses to eat anything green on race days.
famousQuote: "You gotta risk it to get the biscuit. Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in a nail-biting finish, overtaking the leading car on the final lap after a daring pass through Eau Rouge, securing his first major international victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Le Mans with only an hour remaining due to a mechanical failure caused by pushing the car too hard, costing his team a likely victory.
